title: Resize a second window by drag while the first window's terminal streams output: both stay right
why: With two windows open, a live resize of one must refit that window's terminal and PTY while the other keeps drawing its running output (no stall, no blank frame, no jump), and keys must still reach the first window's job afterwards.
source: window life: two windows, resize by drag (holistic-quality.md 1)

steps.text: for i in $(seq 1 200000); do echo out-${nonce}-$i; sleep 0.02; done

steps.title: the first window's terminal streams output
Cmd-Shift-N (a new window, on its New Tab page)
the new window opens; it becomes the key window

Cmd-Shift-N's New Tab key hold (NewTabInputCoordinator.incomingHoldLimit, 4 s) ends: in a capture slot the app is never active, so held keys would be replayed into the first window (NSApp.keyWindow is nil), which no person sees; no state shows the hold's end
Ctrl-` in the new window (New Terminal Tab)
the new window's terminal tab has the focus and a shell
set-up: the second window at 45% x 45% of the screen, right of center
the second window's terminal fits it
drag the second window's corner 250 right and 180 down (button held)
mid-drag: the second window's grid follows, its prompt stays in view; the first window keeps streaming
after the drag: the second window's PTY has its new grid
back to the first window (keys and frames)
the first window still streams and draws its output
the stream stops, the prompt returns
the first window's shell answers and the frame shows it, at the bottom
